message: We’ll design for around 500 PDF invoices a day, up to 10 MB each, with personal data kept in Australia and originals plus extraction audit history retained for 90 days. I’ve proposed Sydney (`au-syd`) for the IBM workflow; service/model availability, backup locations and the accounting API’s processing location remain unverified.

proposal.title: Add Australian residency, invoice limits and retention
proposal.body: Preserve the existing workflow, staff access and accounting connection. Propose Sydney within the requested Australian boundary without recording it as an accepted region decision. Record 10 MB as 10,000,000 bytes; retain 90 days as the requested policy, with backup/version cleanup and deletion timing requiring implementation acceptance. Around 500 invoices per day is a workload input, not a measured throughput result.

next.name: Asynchronous document intake
next.requirements: Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue. Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices. A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API. Use IBM Cloud. Recommend a coherent system and the engineering choices. Ask only a small material business question when needed; do not make me configure the system.

data.label: Staff upload and review
data.description: Existing staff browsers upload PDF invoices, inspect extracted fields alongside source evidence, correct results and submit approval. Browser controls do not grant reviewer authorization; the application enforces membership and permissions.

data.label: Invoice intake and approval
data.description: Proposed composed invoice-workflow delivery unit on IBM Code Engine, with Sydney (au-syd) proposed within the accepted Australian data boundary. Owns browser/API, background worker, isolated PDF/OCR parser, IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL transactional queue/outbox and review state, private versioned IBM Cloud Object Storage originals, IBM Cloud App ID staff sign-in, separate workload identities and regional watsonx extraction. Accepts PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes, interpreting 10 MB as decimal, for an expected workload of around 500 invoices per day; burst capacity remains unmeasured. Invoices may contain personal data and are Confidential. Extracts supplier, invoice date, total and currency with source evidence; failed, uncertain or invalid extraction remains visible in review. Only the parser handles untrusted PDF bytes, without model, database, object-store or accounting identity. Server-side reviewer membership gates approval of the exact result revision and destination operation; edits require renewed approval. Durable operation identities and bounded retries protect repeated delivery; uncertain accounting outcomes are held for reconciliation rather than blindly resent. Retain originals and extraction audit history for 90 days, with scheduled cleanup and reviewed backup/version expiry; the retention clock and final deletion timing remain explicit acceptance details. Documents, extracted data and copies containing them must remain in Australia, including model processing, recovery copies and sensitive diagnostics; no silent overseas fallback. Owns audit history, maintenance, recovery procedures and monitoring tasks. Initial scope remains staff-uploaded PDF invoices, extraction, review and approved accounting submission. Operating ownership remains unresolved. Regional availability of Code Engine, PostgreSQL, object storage, App ID, the selected watsonx model and private connectivity is unverified. Artifact/registry replication geography, model-processing policy, retention behavior, restore, alert delivery, accounting compatibility and the accounting destination's Australian processing boundary require independent acceptance.

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, preserved outside provisioning scope. Receives only reviewer-approved invoice fields through the guarded accounting adapter. Its actual API, authorization, processing/storage country, idempotency durability and reconciliation behavior are unknown. Before sending extracted personal data, establish that the destination and its processing/storage paths satisfy the Australian residency requirement. The destination must implement and independently pass the normalized-action-v1 contract and idempotency acceptance; this diagram does not establish native compatibility. Ambiguous outcomes require reconciliation before another send.

edges.label: HTTPS: sign in, upload PDF, review fields and approve
HTTPS: approved invoice, stable operation ID and receipt reconciliation

requirementDrafts.rationale: Personal data could leave Australia through inference, backups, diagnostics or accounting delivery even when primary storage is Australian. This proposed requirement makes those paths subject to acceptance.
requirementDrafts.basis: “they may contain personal data” and “Keep documents and extracted data in Australia; flag unverified service availability.”
requirementDrafts.statement: Documents and extracted data shall be stored and processed in Australia. Apply this boundary to inference, recovery copies, diagnostics containing those data and accounting delivery. Flag unverified service/model availability and processing geography; do not enable an overseas fallback.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Retention must cover original objects and durable audit records consistently; backup and object-version expiry need acceptance to avoid retaining hidden copies indefinitely.
requirementDrafts.basis: “Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.”
requirementDrafts.statement: The system shall retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days and implement scheduled retention cleanup. Document and test the retention clock, object-version handling and backup expiry before claiming a final deletion deadline.

measure.metric: Original and extraction audit retention period

requirementDrafts.rationale: The stated daily volume informs queue capacity and worker sizing; durable intake must preserve invoices during processing delays. No peak rate or completion deadline was supplied.
requirementDrafts.basis: “around 500 per day” and the existing asynchronous invoice review workflow.
requirementDrafts.statement: Design and qualify asynchronous intake for approximately 500 invoices per day, using durable queueing and recoverable processing. Establish tested burst capacity and processing completion times without treating the daily average as a peak-rate guarantee.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Adds the supplied upload limit while preserving extraction, review and failure visibility. Decimal MB is an explicit engineering interpretation.
requirementUpdates.statement: The system shall accept PDF invoices up to 10 MB (proposed interpretation: 10,000,000 bytes) and persist supplier, invoice date, total and currency in a review queue linked to the original document. Reject oversized input explicitly; failed or uncertain extraction shall remain visible for staff resolution.

decisionUpdates.subject: data.country
decisionUpdates.sourceText: Keep documents and extracted data in Australia

skills.name: Architecture composition and engineering judgment
skills.summary: Choose and compose blocks through responsibility, contracts, state, identity, failure modes and trade-offs; verify the complete system.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: AI architecture and discovery
skills.summary: Clarify outcome, users, existing systems, data ownership and constraints. Evolve the diagram incrementally. Derive functional requirements and propose measurable quality targets as assumptions needing confirmation. Compare clouds against the actual requirements; do not assume an enterprise identity provider or a vendor. Keep proposed and accepted decisions distinct.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: Security and reliability
skills.summary: Check data classification, residency, access boundaries, encryption choices, approval of automated actions, reliability and recovery. A drawn control is not enforcement evidence. Explain missing controls and tests. Propose requirements from the components and paths; mark default targets as suggestions, never existing company policy.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance

skills.name: IBM Cloud architecture guidance
skills.summary: Match watsonx, data services, identity, application runtime and observability to the same requirements used for other clouds. Check region, data residency, model access and IBM plan before pricing. Use a sourced IBM quote; do not substitute an AWS/Azure rate or claim an unsupported deployment is ready.
skills.source: AtMem AI Architect reviewed specialist guidance
